bibliography.title: Calcium phosphate-based anti-infective bone cements: recent trends and future perspectives
bibliography.authors: Liu X, Wang C, Wang H, Wang G, Zhang Y, Zhang Y.

study.research_problem: Bone infection requires local bacterial control while preserving defect filling, mechanical integrity, host-cell safety, degradation, and new-bone formation, but adding antimicrobial functions to calcium-phosphate cement can improve one objective while degrading another.
study.exact_gap: The field lacks a clinically standardized CPC formulation that simultaneously maintains an effective local antimicrobial window, resists biofilm and intracellular infection, limits cytotoxicity/resistance, remains injectable and mechanically adequate, and resorbs in step with bone formation (S009:C01-S011:C04; S019:C01-S020:C05).
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Narratively organize CPC-based anti-infective strategies, including polymers, antibiotics, antimicrobial peptides, therapeutic ions, graphene, iodine, and CPC-calcium-sulfate composites, and outline multifunctional design and translation needs (S001:C01; S012:C01-S020:C05).
study.study_design: Thematic narrative review with descriptive tables and selected examples from in-vitro, animal, case-report, and clinical studies; no reproducible database search, eligibility criteria, screening flow, risk-of-bias assessment, evidence grading, or quantitative synthesis is reported in the packet.
study.sample_or_model: Heterogeneous prior studies spanning cement particles, injectable pastes, scaffolds, implant coatings, multiple antimicrobial agents, cell assays, animal infection models, case reports, and small clinical comparisons.
comparators: CPC versus PMMA or calcium-sulfate cement in selected cited studies
Loaded versus unloaded cement and concentration gradients in selected laboratory/animal studies
CPC-calcium-sulfate composite versus calcium sulfate in one cited clinical comparison
Antibiotic versus non-antibiotic strategies across non-comparable study designs
No review-level common comparator or pooled effect estimate
method_spine: Define infection mechanisms that a local carrier must address.
Map CPC composition, porosity, injectability, strength, degradation, and loading route to clinical use context.
Separate release-control strategies from antibacterial-agent classes.
Track each cited example by evidence level and nearest measured endpoint.
Expose trade-offs among MIC/toxicity window, burst/sustained release, porosity/strength, cytotoxicity/antimicrobial activity, and resorption/bone formation.
Treat intracellular targeting, phages, phototherapy, and immunomodulation as future hypotheses unless directly validated.

verification: The review provides ingredient/intervention/outcome examples in tables and describes plausible release and infection mechanisms, but supplies no systematic-search or duplicate-extraction audit trail (S011:C03-S018:C04).

Internal numerical reporting should be checked against original studies; for example, the reproduced clinical table contains an apparently identical follow-up mean in both groups with P=0.041 (S018:C02).
validation: In-vitro antibacterial, cytotoxicity, release, animal infection, case, and clinical outcomes belong to the cited original studies, not a validation experiment performed by this review.
Clinical examples support feasibility signals for specific formulations and contexts; they do not validate CPCs as a class or establish a universal multifunctional optimum (S013:C02-S018:C04).
sensitivity: The narrative discusses sensitivity to drug-loading route/dose, matrix porosity/crystallinity, polymer content, ion concentration, cement composition, and weight-bearing context (S011:C01-S015:C04).
No formal review-level subgroup, heterogeneity, publication-bias, or sensitivity analysis is performed.
application_prediction: Intracellular targeting, phage delivery, photodynamic/photothermal systems, and immunomodulatory CPCs are forward design directions, not established clinical applications (S020:C01-S020:C05).

primary_outcomes: The review identifies CPC injectability, low-temperature setting, bone-mineral-like chemistry, and porous drug-carrier function, while explicitly noting brittleness and limited strength at weight-bearing sites (S010:C01-S011:C02).

Drug loading and release depend on loading route, dose, pore structure, surface area, crystallinity, polymer swelling/degradation, and matrix affinity; the target is a local concentration above MIC but below toxic levels without a prolonged sub-inhibitory tail (S011:C03-S012:C03).

Antibiotics have the broadest cited evidence, whereas AMPs, ions, graphene, and iodine are supported mainly by heterogeneous laboratory/animal examples and introduce cytotoxicity, stability, or evidence-volume constraints (S013:C01-S017:C01).

CPC-calcium-sulfate composites are presented as a way to balance slow CPC and rapid calcium-sulfate resorption; cited animal, case, and small clinical signals remain formulation-specific and non-pooled (S018:C01-S018:C04).
The review concludes that multifunctionality can compromise cement physicochemical properties, increase manufacturing complexity/cost, and encounter regulatory barriers (S019:C01-S020:C01).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Narrative secondary synthesis containing selected clinical examples but no systematic evidence-quality framework; useful for mechanism and design-variable mapping, not comparative efficacy estimation.

argument_map.central_claim: Anti-infective CPC design is a constrained multi-objective problem: antibacterial exposure, host-cell safety, mechanical/handling performance, porosity, drug release, resorption, and bone repair must be jointly reported, and evidence must remain stratified by formulation and validation level.
data: Selected prior studies of antibiotic, peptide, ion, graphene, iodine, composite-cement, targeting, phage, phototherapy, and immunomodulatory systems (S012:C01-S020:C05).
A clinical-use discussion linking defect size/shape and weight-bearing status to particles, pastes, and supplemental fixation (S011:C01-S011:C02).
argument_map.warrant: A local antimicrobial carrier succeeds only if bacterial control occurs within a safe exposure window without destroying the cement properties and biological/structural functions required in the actual defect.
backing: The review repeatedly notes antibiotic-induced mechanical compromise, silver cytotoxicity, brittleness, mismatched degradation, formulation complexity, cost, and regulatory restrictions (S011:C01; S013:C06; S015:C03-S015:C04; S018:C01; S019:C01-S020:C01).
argument_map.qualifier: Mechanism- and design-oriented narrative synthesis; formulation-specific evidence only.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: No systematic methods establish completeness, study quality, or freedom from selective citation.
In-vitro planktonic/biofilm killing, animal histology, radiographic fill, infection recurrence, and clinical function are different endpoints and cannot be merged as one efficacy construct.
Antibacterial assay controls are not treatment comparators, and cell viability/marker responses do not establish osteoinduction or osseointegration.

Porosity can aid drug transport and tissue access while lowering strength; interconnected macro- and microporosity should be measured rather than assumed from calcium-phosphate particles (S010:C02-S011:C01).
Clinical claims depend on cement chemistry, antimicrobial, dose, infection organism, debridement/fixation, defect, and follow-up.
Future technologies are examples and hypotheses, not recommendations for routine use.

measured: The review itself measures no biological, mechanical, release, animal, or clinical outcomes; its observable product is a thematic organization of cited literature.
Numerical release, antibacterial, cytotoxicity, animal, radiographic, recurrence, and clinical outcomes are measurements reported by individual cited studies (S013:C02-S018:C04).
inferred: CPC pores, additives, and antimicrobial classes are linked to release, antibacterial action, bone formation, and translation through cross-study mechanistic synthesis (S010:C02-S020:C05).
Composite cements are inferred to synchronize resorption and bone formation better than either phase alone, but this is not a universally tested kinetic relationship (S018:C01-S018:C04).
recommended: Standardize formulation, porosity/metrology, mechanical and release protocols, organism/biofilm models, cytotoxicity, degradation, fixation context, and staged animal/clinical outcomes; add direct comparisons and long-term safety.
Test intracellular targeting, phage, phototherapy, and immunomodulation while preserving cement mechanics and host compatibility (S020:C01-S020:C05).
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: Zone of inhibition, CFU reduction, or MIC maintenance supports antibacterial activity under the tested assay, not eradication of chronic human osteomyelitis.
Cell viability, ALP, or osteogenic markers support an in-vitro signal, not osteoinduction, osseointegration, or functional bone restoration.
Radiographic fill/new bone is not direct interface strength or restored weight-bearing capacity.
Drug release duration is useful only relative to organism-specific MIC, host toxicity, spatial distribution, and active-drug stability.
A lower recurrence count in a small formulation-specific study does not establish class superiority.
overclaim_risks: The abstract/introduction call clinical effectiveness and broad osteoconductive/osteoinductive behavior validated more generally than the heterogeneous cited evidence warrants (S001:C01; S009:C01-S010:C02).
Statements that metal-doped CPCs simultaneously provide antimicrobial and bone-regenerative efficacy sometimes rely on cell-count or short animal proxies (S015:C01-S015:C04).
The narrative can make evidence volume appear equivalent across antibiotics, AMPs, ions, graphene, iodine, and emerging systems despite very different validation levels.
The automatic porous-scaffold and animal/clinical cues describe review content, not this article's own experimental design.

section_moves.move: Derive carrier requirements from pathogen persistence mechanisms
section_moves.execution: The review links intracellular residence, OLCN invasion, biofilm, abscess, and diabetic-host factors to limitations of systemic/local treatment (S003:C01-S009:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Start a multifunctional biomaterial paper with the biological/clinical failure mechanisms, then map each design function to a specific barrier rather than listing features.
section_moves.failure_mode: A mechanism list becomes decorative if each barrier is not paired with an outcome and validation model.

section_moves.move: Write the formulation as a multi-objective constraint map
section_moves.execution: The paper connects defect/weight-bearing context, strength, injectability, setting, porosity, loading route, release window, degradation, and additives (S011:C01-S012:C03).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For drug-loaded bone cements, report clinical context, matrix state, loading route, pore/metrology, handling, mechanics, release, antimicrobial threshold, toxicity, and degradation as coupled constraints.
section_moves.failure_mode: Calling one formulation optimal from release or inhibition alone hides mechanical and biological penalties.

section_moves.move: Stratify evidence by agent and validation level
section_moves.execution: Antibiotic examples span in-vitro, animal, case, and clinical data, whereas many alternative agents remain at in-vitro or animal levels (S013:C02-S017:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: In a review table, give each formulation one row per study with study type, comparator, organism, dose, release, mechanics, host response, endpoint, follow-up, and locator; never let a clinical case and cell assay share one undifferentiated success column.
section_moves.failure_mode: A narrative list without search and quality assessment cannot support comparative ranking.

section_moves.move: Make trade-offs and failure modes the synthesis
section_moves.execution: The review identifies burst versus sustained release, MIC versus toxicity/resistance, porosity versus brittleness, antimicrobial loading versus mechanics, and degradation versus bone formation (S011:C01-S018:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Conclude multifunctional-material studies with a benefit-penalty matrix and identify the comparison needed to isolate each claimed function.
section_moves.failure_mode: More functions do not imply a better device when interactions and penalties are untested.

section_moves.move: Separate emerging mechanism from translation gate
section_moves.execution: Intracellular targeting, phages, phototherapy, and immune modulation are paired with safety, stability, physicochemical, cost, and regulatory challenges (S020:C01-S020:C05).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For each emerging platform, write mechanism, nearest evidence, missing discriminator, manufacturing constraint, and clinical validation gate in separate clauses.
section_moves.failure_mode: Future-facing examples become overclaims when promising in-vitro results are phrased as clinical solutions.

author_reported: Multifunctional loading can compromise CPC physicochemical properties; fabrication complexity, cost, cytotoxicity, safety/stability, and regulation restrict translation (S019:C01-S020:C05).
reader_identified: No reported search strategy, date, databases, eligibility criteria, screening, duplicate extraction, risk of bias, evidence grading, or review protocol.
Selected studies mix cement formulations, agents/doses, loading routes, defects, organisms, outcomes, species, and follow-up without a common comparison framework.
Some claims about universal CPC osteoinduction, clinical validation, osseointegration, and optimality exceed the nearest cited endpoint.
No systematic reporting of null/negative studies, adverse events, resistance evolution, mechanical penalties, or publication bias.
Table-level numerical and terminology inconsistencies require verification against originals before citation (S018:C02).
Review cues for animal/clinical/porous scaffolds should not be misclassified as experiments performed by the review authors.
likely_bias_direction: Selective positive examples likely inflate apparent breadth and readiness of multifunctional CPC strategies.
Combining evidence levels may overstate clinical efficacy and understate toxicity, mechanics, and negative studies.
Mechanism-rich narrative may make causal links appear stronger than study-level comparator designs permit.
limitations.scope_boundary: Use this article to map CPC anti-infective design variables, trade-offs, mechanisms, and research gaps; verify every quantitative or efficacy claim in the original study and do not use the review alone to rank formulations or claim clinical effectiveness.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write multifunctional bone-cement design as a coupled constraint map spanning infection mechanism, drug window, toxicity, porosity, handling, mechanics, degradation, fixation, and tissue repair.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Introduction argument spine, Methods design rationale, and Discussion trade-off matrix.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A formulation that maximizes bacterial killing may exceed host toxicity, weaken cement, or release sub-therapeutic drug later.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: For mixed-evidence reviews, stratify every formulation by study type, comparator, organism, dose, endpoint, follow-up, and evidence level before synthesis.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Review evidence matrix and bounded conclusions.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: In-vitro, animal, case, and clinical signals cannot be pooled narratively into a universal efficacy claim.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Bind future biomaterial claims to a five-part gate: mechanism, nearest evidence, untested discriminator, manufacturing/regulatory constraint, and next validation level.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Promising targeting, phage, phototherapy, or immune signals are not clinical recommendations without safety, stability, mechanics, and controlled outcome evidence.

critical_weaknesses: No systematic review method or quality assessment.
Heterogeneous evidence levels and endpoints are narrated together.
Broad osteoinduction, osseointegration, clinical-effectiveness, and optimality wording often outruns formulation-specific evidence.

summary_zh: 这是一篇 CPC 抗感染骨水泥的叙述性设计综述，而不是系统评价或效果荟萃。其真正可迁移价值是把材料开发写成多目标约束：局部药物必须处于 MIC 与宿主毒性之间，同时还要控制爆发释放和亚抑菌尾部，保留注射/凝固/力学性能，并使孔隙、降解和新骨形成相协调。文中混合了体外、动物、病例和小型临床研究，因此每个数字都应回到原始论文核验，不能据此排序药物或水泥类别。最稳健的写法是按配方—剂量—载药方式—孔结构—释药—力学—抗菌—宿主反应—模型层级建立证据矩阵；对细胞内靶向、噬菌体、光疗和免疫调节，则同时写出安全、稳定、制造、成本和监管验证门槛。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed every non-reference packet section and both embedded evidence tables.
Animal, clinical, porous-scaffold, and biological cues describe cited literature rather than an experiment performed by this review.
Use the article as a design/trade-off map and verify quantitative claims against original sources before manuscript citation.
